page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g9ae.2xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance running on the KVM hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9T95 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.25 GHz, providing 8 dedicated vCPUs. Memory allocation is set at 32.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 4.0 GB of memory per core. Dedicated compute allocation ensures predictable CPU resources without virtualization steal time under sustained loads.

Network connectivity features a baseline bandwidth capacity of 6 Gbps. The ecs.g9ae.2xlarge does not include local disk storage or bundled public IPv4 addresses, requiring the configuration of external cloud storage solutions for persistent file systems and operating system volumes. The absence of integrated GPUs or local NVMe drives narrows its focus strictly toward standard compute and network traffic management rather than hardware-accelerated rendering or extreme local I/O operations.

Cost efficiency is aligned with the general-purpose cloud tier, delivering a balanced distribution between processing capability and memory capacity. This hardware profile avoids the price premiums associated with high-memory or dedicated accelerator tiers. The ecs.g9ae.2xlarge is suitable for enterprise application backends, container orchestration nodes, middle-tier web servers, CI/CD runners, and distributed data processing tasks requiring dedicated CPU performance.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g9ae.2xlarge is a general-purpose virtual server configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs and 32.0 GB of RAM, providing a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. Built on x86_64 architecture using an AMD EPYC 9T95 processor clocked at 2.25 GHz under the KVM hypervisor, this instance delivers consistent dedicated CPU execution for diverse enterprise workloads. Networking features a 6 Gbps baseline bandwidth capacity. The instance does not include integrated local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, requiring external cloud block storage for persistent volumes. Operating without burstable CPU throttling or specialized hardware accelerators, the resource allocation provides balanced qualitative cost efficiency for mainstream production deployments. The configuration is appropriate for hosting web application servers, container clusters, background processing queues, enterprise microservices, and continuous integration environments.
